chunk_map.heading: From the three of you to your team
We built good things. We failed to share them well.
An agent's instructions are not the agent
Access is easy; absorption is scarce
What would have to be true for your team to switch?
On Monday the team decides, not the three of you

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 3 'Access is easy' l.4 "People can reach the agent" - 'the agent' resolves to 'Your agent' / 'An agent's instructions' named in chunk 2 (header + l.4); chunk 5 l.4 'the three of you' is the trio of the module arc, earned in chunk 1 l.8.
Closest: chunk 1 l.6 byline names the essay by title and author, not by position; no 'the opening lecture' style pointers anywhere in the 5 slides.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 2 l.6 'the memory you built up from your interviews and tickets' - generic work the trio did, not a 'the X you did/saw' beat; no named beat referenced. Module arc carve-out also covers 'the three of you worked out'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 l.4-8 is a quote slide, but it carries a self-sufficient claim (sharing is harder than building) plus a bridge sentence at l.8.
Closest: chunk 4 header is a question; body l.6 answers it ('The answers come back small and specific') - true summary. Chunk 5 header 'On Monday the team decides' matches l.4 and l.8.

Closest: chunk 4 l.6 'Not how do we get the team to adopt this? but what would have to be true...' is a single contrast recast as one declarative, not Not-X-Not-Y-Z; 'It lands where they already look. It is right the first time they try it. Someone they trust has used it' is three concrete items with varied openers, not anaphora; no superlatives, no number+retraction, no empty verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 3 'absorption' (header, l.4-6) is ordinary organisational vocabulary defined on the slide; grep of body for surface/firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood returns nothing in the 5 slides.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No bold anywhere in the composed body; budget of <=1 bold per slide is met.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: lecture is 5 standalone include lines (l.3-11); each slide file is inlined as its own ## by read-curriculum.js (5 headings in expanded view), so no phase-less prose is dropped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: check-slide-numbering.js --file -> 'OK - 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; no Phase/Step headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: check-slide-deixis.js --file -> 'OK - 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'; 'On Monday' is a time, not a position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links; only structural include-links

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 4 header is a question, not a claim (l.2 of slide file); rule binds law/consolidation slides and the lecture's other four headers are claims; chunk 4 is a framing question, so no declaration is being mislabeled.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 5 l.8 'Their changes are how it becomes theirs.' - adds a move (expect and welcome edits), does not restate the header; chunk 1 l.4 repeats the header's two sentences but as the attested verbatim essay quote per its maintainer STATUS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 4 retitled to 'your team' per its STATUS; body l.4-6 was rewritten for the trio's proposal ('Your proposal is not competing with nothing') and answers the new header, no inherited old-job bullets.

notes: Body is five slide-file includes; read via read-curriculum.js. Accept-notes in maintainer block: none relevant to slides class (Quality line and STATUS only). All 17 rules were in the brief (prefill parked none).
